summary: The note explores how gamification, the use of game mechanics like points, badges and leaderboards, is being integrated into education to boost engagement, motivation and retention among digitally native students. It covers the 'Quest for Knowledge' app, Dr. Emily Roberts' longitudinal study, student and teacher perspectives, and challenges such as budgets and teacher training. It also notes gamification's use beyond classrooms and upcoming events like the GamifyEDU fair.
one_line: Gamification in education boosts student engagement and retention, but demands teacher training, funding and attention to equity as adoption grows.
key_facts: Since the beginning of the 2023 academic year, educators have been integrating game design elements into teaching to boost engagement and knowledge retention.

Dr. Emily Roberts, an educational psychologist at the University of Silicon Beach, defines gamification as "the incorporation of game elements, such as point scoring, competition with others, and rules of play, into non-game contexts - including school curricula".
The 'Quest for Knowledge' app launched on September 15, 2023, at the National Education Technology Conference, covering subjects from Algebra to World History.
Sofia Martinez, 16, of New Horizons High School, became top player in her class on the 'Race Through Time' leaderboard and says she remembers much more history.
Dr. Roberts' longitudinal study, initiated October 3, 2023, involves over 500 students across various age groups.
The study found gamified learning environments are often associated with increased motivation and engagement.
Gamification supports visual, auditory and kinesthetic learners, and this multi-sensory engagement leads to greater retention and understanding.
Keeping pace with technological advancements can strain school budgets and teacher training programs.
Michael Thompson, an award-winning educator at Digital Frontier Middle School, said in a December 1, 2023 interview, "There's a steep learning curve."
Laura Diaz, co-founder of the Educational Gaming Initiative (EGI), announced on January 20, 2024 a partnership with tech giants to introduce a state-of-the-art educator training program.
On February 11, 2024, a Code for Tomorrow hackathon had young developers create gamified solutions for community issues such as recycling education and neighborhood wellness programs.
The 'GamifyEDU' fair is scheduled for April 7, 2024, bringing together students, developers and educators.
Accessibility, equity in education and evolving teaching methods are named as critical hurdles ahead.
